title: Rizal Provincial Library System - Updated System Flowcharts
basis: Current application source and existing regression coverage. These diagrams document implemented workflows; they do not certify every production integration.

flows.title: Login and Role Routing
flows.description: Shows password or Face ID sign-in, account checks, first-login password replacement, and routing to the stored member or librarian role.

nodes.label: Enter email or Member ID and password
Capture one live face; run PAD and enrolled-face matching
Identity, active account and portal role accepted?
Show error; retry or use password / supervised assistance
Open member dashboard or permitted next page
Open librarian dashboard or permitted next page

notes: Public catalog browsing requires no account. The current website registers members through librarians; it has no public registration form.
Face ID is optional and requires existing enrollment. Failed or unavailable live-face verification does not grant access.
Member and librarian are the two stored roles. A website login does not record entrance attendance.

flows.title: Borrower Navigation
flows.description: Shows navigation among the member dashboard, book discovery, My Reservations, and Profile.

nodes.label: Dashboard: loans, due notices, activity and goals
Browse Books: shelves, search and favorites (2.3.3)
My Reservations: selection, ready books and queue (2.3.4 / 2.3.15)
Profile: contact details, photo and security (2.3.13)
Revoke current session and clear browser sign-in

notes: The reserved-count button in Browse Books opens My Reservations.
Borrowers can report a loan issue from the dashboard; only librarians complete physical borrow and return transactions.

flows.title: Browse Books and Add to Reservation Cart
flows.description: Shows public and member discovery, book details, and selection for later reservation confirmation.

nodes.label: Open public catalog or member Browse Books
Search title or author; choose genre, shelf or sort
No duplicate and a slot remains?
Show duplicate, capacity or pending-request message
Add title to local reservation selection

notes: Adding a selection does not hold stock, create a loan, or save a confirmed reservation.
Landing-page searches open the public catalog and highlight matching title or author text. Member Featured shelves scroll sideways; the desktop public catalog uses a vertical grid.

flows.title: Reservation Checkout and Five-Book Limit
flows.description: Shows authenticated batch confirmation, explicit queue agreement, the combined five-book allowance, and safe retry handling.

nodes.label: Load selection, existing reservations and remaining slots
Agree to queue each unavailable title?
Save confirmation request ID and submit batch
Show quota, overdue, duplicate or availability conflict
Keep original request; retry same confirmation safely
Save whole batch: ready or queued
Clear selection; refresh reservations and slots

notes: The current confirmation endpoint does not request a face scan. At physical pickup, librarians identify the member by Face ID or supervised manual ID.
Five-book limit = active/overdue loans + ready reservations + queued reservations + new selections. The server rechecks the limit and eligibility.
Unavailable titles require explicit queue agreement. Ready reservations have a 24-hour pickup deadline; no exact physical copy is allocated by reservation.

flows.title: Staff Logging and Entrance Attendance
flows.description: Shows PIN-controlled attendance scanning, live-face validation, and time-in/time-out for a distinct encounter.

nodes.label: Display privacy notice and start camera
No successful attendance; show assistance message
Keep existing state; ignore repeated visible frames
Show confirmed state and attendance log

notes: This is entrance attendance for recognized enrolled accounts, not a separate payroll or staff scheduling module.
The current station client debounces repeated frames and marks distinct encounters. Legacy clients retain the configured timing rules.
Station PIN access does not issue account login cookies. Scanning pauses when the page is hidden, and failed connections are not saved for offline replay.

flows.title: Add Book and QR Code Generation
flows.description: Shows manual or ISBN-assisted book entry, optional descriptions, validation, physical-copy creation, and label preparation.

nodes.label: Review title, author, category, year, shelf and copy count
Optionally add online description or write a note
Save title and create physical copies with unique QR codes
Upload optional cover; report cover-only failure separately
Open Print QR; download exact-copy labels (2.3.23)

notes: A description is optional, public catalog text. Manual descriptions are supported when no online description is available.
Each physical copy receives its own identity. QR image download/reprinting does not create more copies.
If the book saves but its cover fails, retry only the cover upload. Resolve an unknown save outcome before submitting another book.

flows.title: Borrow Transaction
flows.description: Shows member identification, automatic selection from ready reservations, optional scanning for walk-ins, and reviewed lending.

nodes.label: Identify member using Face ID or supervised manual ID
Load member slots, ready reservations and queued requests
Select Add to list; system chooses an available physical copy
Scan QR or enter book code for walk-in / extra title
Explicitly choose copy when legacy code is ambiguous
Review titles, exact copies and due-date preview
Show rejected item; keep confirmed successes
Create loan; update copy and stock; fulfill applicable reservation
Handle each item and unknown outcomes (2.3.27)
Show results; hand over confirmed copies

notes: Ready reservations use Add to list without mandatory QR scanning or code selection. Staff may change the copy before review and must hand over the copy shown. Queued requests are not ready loans.
Selections and scans do not commit a loan. A ready reservation converts to a loan without consuming a second slot.
Multi-book submissions are sequential independent requests. No silent copy substitution occurs if a selected copy becomes unavailable.
Final server checks cover account status, overdue loans, the combined allowance, ready-hold capacity, duplicate title loans and exact-copy availability.

flows.title: Return Transaction
flows.description: Shows exact-copy lookup, explicit selection of ambiguous legacy loans, review, and updating the original loan.

nodes.label: Scan physical-copy QR or enter code
Show invalid / missing code; correct entry
Choose the exact outstanding loan for a legacy code
Add original transaction and copy to return list
Review borrower, title and physical copy
Original loan and copy still valid?
Show rejection; do not mark returned
Update original loan to returned; preserve borrow date and copy ID
Restore available stock; assess late fine if applicable
Handle per-item results and unknown outcomes (2.3.27)

notes: A return closes the original loan; it does not create an unrelated return row or erase borrowing history.
Return mode starts with book lookup and can contain different borrowers. Members do not self-confirm physical returns.
An assessed fine is not payment collection. The current interface hides fine panels.

flows.title: Report Generation
flows.description: Shows authorized reporting, Philippine-time filters, paged previews, and validated exports or print output.

nodes.label: Choose usage, patrons, circulation, collection, acquisitions or inventory
Set date basis, Philippine dates and category filters
Show error or empty result; revise when needed
Read authorized logs, transactions, member and inventory data
Build summaries, charts and paged records
Choose scope and CSV, Excel, PDF or Print
Preview current and export within limits?
Generate safe output for selected scope

notes: Monthly PDF uses its own Month and Year controls. Report previews and exports preserve applied filters, not unsaved draft changes.
Period circulation counts use borrow dates including returned loans. Current overdue and stock figures are snapshots. Export scope and row limits must be checked.
Reports are librarian-only. Acquisition reporting needs its separate schema upgrade; these diagrams do not establish that every production prerequisite is complete.

flows.title: Due Books Monitoring
flows.description: Shows refresh-time overdue evaluation, due-date filtering, librarian review, and the link to physical return processing.

nodes.label: Refresh outstanding loans; synchronize overdue status
Choose All, Overdue or Due Soon
Show overdue status, days late and assessed amount
Display borrower, title, copy and due date
Continue monitoring or contact member through approved process

notes: Due Soon is the next three days. The default All due-book query includes overdue loans and loans due within seven days; broader loan records are separate.
Overdue loans can prevent new borrowing. Email/SMS overdue reminders are currently unavailable, so this chart does not claim automatic message delivery.

flows.title: Member Registration and Temporary Password Delivery
flows.description: Shows librarian registration with optional identification uploads, email-first credential delivery, and supervised fallback.

nodes.label: Enter verified name; optional email, phone, location and ID upload
Required fields, contacts and optional upload valid?
Create Member ID; hash 10-character temporary password; require replacement
Do not display temporary password to librarian
Display same temporary password for private librarian handoff
Member signs in and changes password (2.3.1 / 2.3.12)

notes: Government ID upload is optional. If supplied, private upload validation still applies.
SMS is selected only when no email is supplied. Failed email delivery does not automatically switch to the phone. Missing or failed delivery falls back to private librarian handoff.
Provider acceptance is not proof that a message reached the inbox or handset. Entered contacts remain unverified until the separate email verification procedure.

flows.title: Forgotten Password and Librarian-Assisted Recovery
flows.description: Shows recovery through a previously verified email or supervised librarian reset when email recovery is unavailable.

nodes.label: Enter email or RPL Member ID
Request reset code without exposing account existence
Visit librarian for supervised identity check
Librarian resets password and privately provides temporary credential
Sign in and replace temporary password (2.3.12)
Retrieve six-digit code from verified mailbox
Enter code and valid new password
Show generic failure or waiting-period message
Save new password; consume code; revoke prior sessions
Return to sign-in with new password

notes: Self-service recovery uses a previously verified email. A phone number or registration SMS does not enable SMS password recovery.
Public responses and errors avoid confirming which accounts exist. Code expiry, resend limits and attempt limits remain enforced.
Librarian reset credentials can have a different length from the 10-character initial-registration password.

flows.title: First-Login and Voluntary Password Change
flows.description: Shows mandatory replacement of temporary passwords and authenticated password changes.

nodes.label: Enter current password, new password and confirmation
New values match and satisfy password policy?
Account active and current password correct?
Hash and save new password; clear temporary-password flag
Revoke all prior sessions and unused reset codes
Create replacement session for this browser
Open permitted member or librarian page

notes: New passwords require 8-128 characters including at least one digit.
Until a required replacement succeeds, ordinary protected actions are blocked. Session/profile retrieval, password change and logout remain available.

flows.title: Profile Details and Optional Profile Photo
flows.description: Shows permitted member contact edits, a locked verified name, and adding, changing or removing an avatar.

nodes.label: Load own profile; show verified name as read-only
Choose Add / Change photo and select image
Image file and upload ownership valid?
Store private avatar; attach to own profile
Photo removable with verified storage ownership?
Remove private photo and clear avatar reference
Show error; retain last confirmed data

notes: Members cannot change their verified name in the form or by sending a different name to the server. Name corrections require library assistance.
A profile photo is optional and separate from face-recognition enrollment. Removing an avatar does not delete the Face ID template.
Only confirmed changes refresh the interface. Invalid or unavailable storage operations do not report a successful removal.

flows.title: Email Change and Contact Verification
flows.description: Shows password-confirmed email changes and separate verification before the address can be used for recovery.

nodes.label: Enter new email and current password
Password correct and email valid / available?
Save email as unverified; invalidate obsolete reset codes
Select Verify Email; confirm current password
Code valid, unused and bound to saved email?

notes: Typing an email during registration or profile editing does not verify ownership.
A changed email remains unverified until the purpose/contact-bound code succeeds. Never publish verification codes in documentation or screenshots.

flows.title: Reservation Queue, Pickup, Cancellation and Expiry
flows.description: Shows the lifecycle of ready and queued reservations, including FIFO promotion and cancellation.

nodes.label: Mark Pending in FIFO queue; no stock held
Capacity freed by return, cancellation or expiry?
Keep queue position; wait for a later policy refresh
Cancel expired ready hold on policy synchronization
Release title capacity; promote next eligible request
Refresh reservation list and remaining slots

notes: Only ready reservations hold title-level capacity. Pending requests do not allocate stock, and no reservation guarantees a particular physical copy.
Expiry/promotion runs when relevant requests or stock-changing operations synchronize policy; there is no claim of a continuously running expiry scheduler.
Both ready and queued reservations count toward the combined five-book allowance. Refreshing a page does not extend a pickup deadline.

flows.title: Inventory Editing, Stock Adjustment and Title Deletion
flows.description: Shows updating book metadata or covers, safe stock changes, and history-protected title deletion.

nodes.label: Edit allowed metadata, description, shelf or copy total
Save metadata; create new copies or retire eligible excess copies
Store cover and attach to existing title
No protected loan or reservation history?
Delete permitted title; clean unused cover

notes: Reducing stock retires eligible physical copies; it does not delete or recycle their QR identities. Borrowed copies and ready-reservation capacity remain protected.
View details is read-only. Books with historical loan or reservation dependencies cannot be casually deleted.
Category review has its own workflow (2.3.28). Acquisition metadata is maintained through Reports, not an Acquisitions button in the inventory row.

flows.title: ISBN Lookup and Workbook Book Import
flows.description: Shows multiple ISBN-assisted additions and complete-record XLSX import with separate results for valid, duplicate and rejected rows.

nodes.label: Librarian opens Add Book import tools
Look up metadata; preview found and missing titles
Review selected entries and correct metadata
Submit selected books with stable request identities
Import valid new rows; skip duplicate ISBNs; record row errors
Create unique physical-copy QR identities for imported titles
Show added, skipped and failed results
Resolve unknown save outcome before retry (2.3.27)
Show validation error; correct original file

notes: Full inventory import uses XLSX; legacy XLS must be converted. The current server limit is 10 MB. ISBN-only extraction/lookup is a different workflow.
A workbook can report partial row errors. Preserve successful results; do not assume that one bad row rolls back every imported book.
Retryable workbook requests are bound to the original file fingerprint and request ID. Acquisition-metadata CSV/XLSX import is separate (2.3.25).

flows.title: Member Status, Password Reset and Account Removal
flows.description: Shows supervised account administration with separate status, reset and deletion actions.

nodes.label: Search and select the correct member
Save status; revoke sessions when suspended
Generate temporary credential; revoke prior sessions; require replacement
Provide displayed credential privately to member
Choose Delete account; confirm librarian password
Show restriction; resolve loans, identity or storage issue
Remove permitted private data; disable account; retain protected history

notes: A librarian password is required for destructive member/face deletion. Account deletion is blocked while books remain outstanding.
Member account removal follows the implemented soft-deletion and private-file ownership checks; it is not arbitrary deletion of lending history.
Resetting a member password is distinct from registration email/SMS delivery. Use the credential actually returned for the reset operation.

flows.title: Librarian-Assisted Face Enrollment and Face Removal
flows.description: Shows supervised enrollment or replacement with live-face and duplicate-account checks, plus explicit face-data removal.

nodes.label: Enroll / replace or delete Face ID?
Start camera; capture a clear live-face image
Show failure; do not replace existing enrollment
Create protected recognition template and save enrollment
Choose Delete face data; enter librarian password
Delete stored face templates and associated face snapshots; revoke member sessions

notes: Enrollment is librarian-assisted and distinct from a profile photo. A failed PAD/quality check must not become a successful enrollment.
Duplicate-face checks prevent enrollment to another account. Existing recognition compatibility and encrypted biometric storage remain in place.
Face-data removal does not delete loan history or the entire member account. It is a separate explicit operation.

flows.title: Recommendations, Trending and Favorites
flows.description: Shows history-dependent Featured shelves, favorites, and genre sorting without inventing a star-rating feature.

nodes.label: Load recommendations from member activity and similar items
Use content / popularity fallback where needed
Show What's new and Books we love shelves
Save or remove own favorite after server confirmation
Choose genre / All Books; select Trending, Newest, Most loved or Title
View details or add to selection (2.3.3)

notes: Members with borrowing history see Recommended for you above Trending. New members begin with Trending. Featured collections scroll sideways.
Books we love and Most loved use recorded favorites; there is no star-rating or separate editorial-review feature.
Recommendations are calculated on demand with collaborative, content and popularity fallbacks. The system does not claim a separately trained model or measured reader accuracy.

flows.title: Reading Activity, Goals and Personal Transcript
flows.description: Shows viewing recorded reading/visit information, saving goals, and downloading the account-owned transcript.

nodes.label: Load own loans, reading statistics, activity and goals
Review recorded borrowing, genres and library visits
Select Set Goals; enter books, genres and visit targets
Request own transcript through supported API service
Authenticated owner and report request valid?

notes: Visits are attendance sessions, not proof that a particular book was read. Charts summarize recorded activity.
Transcripts are owner-scoped. Members cannot download another member profile or transcript by changing an identifier.
The owner-scoped transcript API exists, but the current member pages do not show a transcript download button. That branch describes the supported service.

flows.title: Loan Issue Reports and In-App Notifications
flows.description: Shows member reporting of a current loan problem and librarian review of the resulting in-app notification.

nodes.label: Choose damaged, wrong book, lost or other; add optional note
Loan is outstanding and owned by current member?
Show rejection; do not create report
Librarian opens notifications and reviews issue
Mark notification read or mark all own notices read

notes: Submitting an issue is not a return, copy replacement, fine settlement or payment. Book-condition photo capture is not implemented.
Members also receive their own in-app notices, such as reservation status updates, and can mark them read. Read status is account-scoped.
No email/SMS delivery is implied by an in-app notice.

flows.title: Physical-Copy QR Label Download and Bulk Export
flows.description: Shows individual PNG labels, selected-copy PDFs, and complete matching-copy exports with bounded batches.

nodes.label: Search title, author or physical-copy QR
Select copies; Select Visible affects current page only
Fetch bounded label batches and count manifest
Build ZIP after all batches succeed
Show error; preserve selection and offer retry
Print and attach each exact-copy label

notes: A printed code identifies one physical copy. Reprinting does not add stock, change copy identity, or record a loan.
Complete matching export uses label batches of 200 and fails visibly if any expected identity or batch is missing. Do not treat an interrupted download as complete.

flows.title: Appearance Settings and Entrance Station PIN Replacement
flows.description: Shows browser appearance preferences and password-confirmed replacement of the staff station PIN.

nodes.label: Open applicable appearance controls or librarian Settings
Librarian checks station PIN configured status
Enter current librarian password and repeat a new 6-12 digit PIN
Password correct and PIN values valid / matching?
Store only protected PIN hash; activate new station PIN
Older stations fail next PIN check; unlock with new PIN

notes: Only librarians manage the station PIN. The existing PIN is never displayed; replacement requires the librarian password, not the old PIN.
A configured database PIN takes precedence over the server fallback and is checked on each station request. Station PINs and account passwords serve different purposes.

flows.title: Acquisition Metadata Entry and Import
flows.description: Shows recording verified acquisition details on existing physical copies through the reporting workspace.

nodes.label: Enter numeric physical-copy ID; look up and verify title
Enter verified source, date, donor / supplier, cost and reference
Prepare CSV / XLSX metadata file; upload for preview
File and all referenced copy IDs valid?
Review replacements; confirm Apply acquisition records
Copy data and version still valid?
Show errors or changed record; reload / preview again
Save acquisition metadata for existing copies

notes: This reporting workflow requires the separate reporting schema. It is not the removed Acquisition details section of Add Book.
Acquisition imports are limited to 500 rows and 1 MB. Blank imported cells clear existing acquisition fields; preview does not save anything.
Metadata refers to existing physical-copy IDs, not a printed QR string. It does not create stock or reassign physical-copy codes.

flows.title: Librarian Workspace, Dashboard and Navigation
flows.description: Shows the initially hidden sidebar, dashboard summaries and access to each librarian workspace.

nodes.label: Open Dashboard; load authorized summaries and charts
Open menu icon to reveal hidden sidebar
Browse Books / Add Book / Print QR (2.3.6, 2.3.16, 2.3.23)
Sign out; revoke current browser session

notes: The sidebar starts hidden on desktop and mobile. Selecting navigation opens the chosen workspace without changing its authorization requirements.
Dashboard notifications and shortcuts link to the relevant workflows. A summary card is not itself a circulation submission.

flows.title: Safe Submission, Partial Results and Unknown Outcome Recovery
flows.description: Shows how reservation, inventory and circulation writes preserve request identity and avoid accidental duplicate actions.

nodes.label: Save original payload and account-scoped request ID
Submit online; do not treat scan or local selection as success
Stop further dependent submissions; preserve pending request
Recover saved request using original ID
Inventory / circulation: look up saved receipt; explicitly retry same key if needed
Reservation: retry exact saved confirmation batch
Keep unknown state; request assistance without inventing success
Show definitive rejection and unattempted items
Show committed result; preserve earlier confirmed successes

notes: Do not clear pending recovery information, invent a new key, or infer success from a similar-looking loan. An unknown result is not a confirmed failure.
Circulation lists send independent sequential requests; earlier successes remain valid. Reservation confirmation is an atomic batch.
There is no durable offline queue or automatic write replay. Recovery and retry require a server connection and the original operation identity.

flows.title: Category Normalization and Librarian Review
flows.description: Shows automatic server category mapping and the Add Book review panel for unresolved imported labels.

nodes.label: New or imported category label received
Check saved override or supported category mapping
Save normalized category and visible catalog state
Preserve original label; mark unresolved book hidden
Librarian opens Add Book: Category review panel
Select supported master category; submit resolution
Apply category override to hidden books with exact original label
Make resolved books available to category lists and catalog

notes: Raw labels are reconciled to the supported genre vocabulary. Unresolved books retain the original label and remain hidden until an authorized resolution.
The Category review panel appears on Add Book. Choosing a master category resolves hidden books with the same exact original label; a suggestion alone does not save a resolution.
